_doc: Rules whose pandas twin and SQL pack differ on the parity dataset. scope: all = any size (asserted exactly on the 2x3 pytest dataset); stress_only = only shows on longer datasets; edge = only on the edge profile. Read by open_fdd.parity, tests/parity and scripts/nf/gen_cookbook.py. expected: the pinned L1 fault-hour delta (SQL vs pandas, all equipment) and tolerance per canonical dataset (profile/seed/equips/days); the stress run fails when an observed delta leaves its band (#1590).

differences.reason: Small residual left after #1642; not yet attributed.
pandas applies the rule's startup delay after the proof turns on; the SQL has no startup holdoff yet (#1646).
pandas proves equipment/cooling from typed roles (mechanical_proof_mask, equipment_type); SQL ORs chiller status / valve

pandas applies the hydronic proof gate with the 600 s startup holdoff; the SQL has no startup holdoff yet (#1646). The tower fan and chilled-water command are boolean, so the on-window is wide enough for that holdoff to show on the 2x3 set as well.

pandas applies the hydronic proof gate with the 600 s startup holdoff; the SQL has no startup holdoff yet (#1646). The tower fan and chilled-water command are boolean, so the on-window is wide enough for that holdoff to show on the 2x3 set as well.

Jittered timestamps (#1642): the weather join itself now matches. pandas joins the raw weather readings as-of (runner.WEB_ASOF_BOUND_SECONDS = 1500 s), as SQL does, which took the edge 4x3 delta from 15.24 h to 0.34 h (MECH-OAT-1 went to 0 and is no longer listed). The remaining 0.34 h on edge AHU-1 is not yet attributed; basic (on-grid) datasets match exactly.

Same cause as FC8: the series begins with the fan already running (edge DST-week start is 18:00 local); pandas applies its 600 s operational startup holdoff at the first sample, SQL does not (verified by trimming the first 6 h of rows).
Edge profile only: after a data gap pandas re-applies its 600 s startup delay; the SQL has no startup holdoff (#1646). Basic datasets match.

Series starts with the fan already running (edge DST-week start is 18:00 local): pandas applies its 600 s operational startup holdoff at the first sample, SQL has none, so SQL confirms one 5-minute sample earlier. Verified: trimming the first 6 h of rows makes SQL equal pandas.
Same cause as FC8: the series begins with the fan already running; pandas holds off 600 s from the first sample, SQL does not (verified by trimming the start).

Planted out-of-range zone_air_temperature (80 degC): the pandas quality layer marks those samples OUT_OF_RANGE and excludes them, SQL computes zone_air_temperature - discharge_air_temperature on the value as given and faults.

documented in sql/fdd/KNOWN_DIFFERENCES.md: pandas uses profile/median/persistence logic, SQL two consecutive exceedances

role names, threshold and missing input are aligned (#1588: contract roles hot-water- / chilled-water-reset-request-sum, fault at request sum <= request_lo, an absent request sum is not assessed on either side). Residual: pandas applies its hydronic proof gate with the 600 s startup holdoff, SQL has no startup holdoff, so SQL confirms one 5-minute sample earlier per pump start; matches on the 2 x 3 and 4 x 3 datasets, differs on the 8 x 7 run

pandas applies its hydronic proof gate with the 600 s startup holdoff; the SQL has no startup holdoff yet (#1646). SQL confirms one 5-minute sample earlier per pump start. The boolean plant command makes that sample visible on the 2 x 3 set as well.

Two input-handling differences: (1) NULL zone_air_temperature cells: SQL drops NULL rows (WHERE zone_air_temperature IS NOT NULL) and holds the previous sample's state across the null run, pandas scores a NULL as not faulted; (2) planted out-of-range zone_air_temperature (80 degC): the pandas quality layer marks it OUT_OF_RANGE and excludes it, SQL scores the value as given.

Duplicate (equipment, timestamp) rows: SQL scores the rows as delivered, the reference de-duplicates first (the input contract is one row per timestamp). Verified: de-duplicating the rows before SQL makes SQL equal pandas.
pandas applies the rule's startup delay after the proof turns on; the SQL has no startup holdoff yet (#1646).

pandas operational gate holds a fan-running rule for startup_delay_seconds=600 after the fan proves on, SQL has no startup holdoff: a fault already present at fan start is confirmed one 5-minute sample earlier in SQL per fan start (0.1667 h over the two fan starts of the 8-equipment 7-day run); with the gate off pandas equals SQL

Gap handling: SQL flags |outdoor_air_intake_temperature - previous sample| above the fixed limit whatever the time between samples, pandas scales the limit by the sample gap (limit x dt/poll), so a real change across a >2 h gap is a spike in SQL only.
